8. Put only the JSON object after the '## Answer' line — no markdown code fences, and nothing after the JSON.

Question kind: M7_Invariants

Question:
Use the full test suite in `tests/qa/testcase.py`, class `TestConditionsEvolveResultDictChronologicalMonotonicitySuiteQA` (21 tests). Each test constructs one or more `cfnlint.context.conditions._conditions.Conditions` instances via `Conditions.create_from_instance(...)` (using `Fn::Equals`, `Fn::And`, `Fn::Or`, `Fn::Not`, and `Condition: Name` source shapes, with parameters that may carry `AllowedValues`) and calls `Conditions.evolve(status)` with various `status` payloads -- including empty status (line-105 short-circuit), idempotent same-status (line-117 short-circuit), single-condition, multi-condition, all-True, all-False, alternating, conflicting AllowedValues (raises `Unsatisfiable` after partial dict build), high-volume distinct payloads, chained evolves, and runs across multiple independent `Conditions` instances. Inside `Conditions.evolve` (file `src/cfnlint/context/conditions/_conditions.py`), the function constructs a fresh local dict `conditions = {}` at line 119 and progressively assigns `conditions[condition] = value.evolve(status=s)` at line 124 once per iteration of `for condition, value in self.conditions.items():`. Sample two variables at every Python `line` event of `Conditions.evolve` across the entire test run, in chronological order across ALL frames: the freshly-built local dict `conditions` (observed via its length) and the input parameter dict `status` (observed via its length). Frames that take either of the two early-return branches (`if not status: return self` at line 105, `if all_same: return self` at line 117) never bind `conditions` and contribute zero observations. Considering only events at which `conditions` is bound, what is the monotonic relationship of the resulting `len(conditions)` sequence (in chronological order across ALL frames in the test run)? Return JSON as `{\"monotonicity\": <label>}` where `<label>` is one of `\"Strictly Increasing\"`, `\"Strictly Decreasing\"`, `\"Non-Decreasing\"`, `\"Non-Increasing\"`, or `\"None\"`.

Template answer (must match exactly):
{"monotonicity":"str"}

- files/tests/qa/testcase.py
